newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN TAKE ONE-GAME LEAD.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN TAKE ONE-GAME LEAD.

text.p: Sweden beat Canada 3-2 on Sunday to take a one-game lead in the best-of-three final of the ice hockey world championship.
Marcus Thuresson scored what proved to be the winning goal with just under four minutes to play.
Canadian netminder Sean Burke stopped Magnus Svensson on a breakaway but could not control the rebound as Thuresson lifted the loose puck over the sprawling goaltender to put Sweden ahead 3-1.
"The puck just dropped down right in front of me," said Thuresson. "I just happened to be there and flipped it home."
With Burke pulled in favour of an extra attacker, Anson Carter deflected Keith Primeau's pass past Tommy Salo to cut the deficit to 3-2 with 38 seconds left.
But the Canadians could not get the equaliser.
"I think we played about up to 80 percent of our potenial offensively but defensively we were almost perfect," Swedish coach Kent Forsberg said.
"The first two periods were like a boxing match with two contenders feeling each other out.
"We played a little better as a team then Canada did and took better advantage of our scoring chances. That is why we won today."

Canadian coach Andy Murray, whose team must win game two on Tuesday to force a deciding game on Wednesday, said: "I didn't know before this game started if I liked this format but after this game I think I like playing the best-of-three."
"We didn't play as good a game as we're capable of playing yet the score was 3-2," said Murray. "We took some bad penalties, especially against Sweden who have such a good power play.
"The best way to kill penalties against Sweden is not to take any.
"We tried to tell our players that all the time but it's just difficult because the game is called differently over here."

"They're very patient, very good and to beat a team like that you can't make the mistakes we did," said Murray. "Even thought we didn't play that well, we still had a chance at the end and that's encouraging."
In the first period the teams traded power play goals.
Mark Recchi of the Montreal Canadiens put Canada ahead 1-0 when he deflected Brian McCabe's slapshot through a crowd in front of the Sweden net.
Jonas Hoglund of the Calgary Flames replied for the Swedes, picking up a rebound at the side of the Canadian net and snapping a wrist-shot past Burke.
Niklas Sundblad's breakaway goal, set up by a perfect feed from Marcus Ragnarsson, accounted for all the scoring in the second period as Sweden took a 2-1 lead.
